description.narrative: Insatsen kompletterar Bangladesh regerings arbete med att fortsatt bygga upp arbetsstyrkan av barnmorskor, där UNFPA bedöms ha komparativa fördelar.
The intervention will complement the work of the Government of Bangladesh in contune developing midwifery workforce in which UNFPA has comparative advantage.

The main objective of the intervention is to improve sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and reduce maternal and neonatal mortality through strengthening the midwifery-led continuum of high-quality comprehensive integrated SRHR services with a special focus on the most vulnerable women and girls of Bangladesh, equally in development, humanitarian and climate vulnerable settings. The three main suggested outcomes are:
Outcome 1: Improved professional capacity of midwives to provide comprehensive and sustainable SRHR services including quality routine and emergency maternity care services.
Outcome 2: Improved Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEmONC) and Comprehensive eEmergency Obstetric and Neonatal Care (CEmONC) services available in Sida target districts through professional midwives and interdisciplinary teams.
Outcome 3: Improved availability of high-quality, sustainable, human rights-based comprehensive and integrated SRHR information and services provided through professional midwives.
The project is implemented in the five most vulnerable districts in the country, covering 31 upzilas(sub-districts)These districts are adversely affected by climate-change, natural hazards, remoteness and inaccessibility due to poor infrastructure.
The project aims to build sustainable structures and capacity at the national and district-levels to introduce and scale up midwifery-led SRHR services, with climate-change adaptation and resilience as important components of the midwifery-led care (MLC) model. Particularly, the project strives to demonstrate the effectiveness of operationalizing government health facilities closest to the community i.e., Union Health and Family Welfare Centres (UHFWC), with the existing physical infrastructure for providing maternity care and other SRHR services through midwives. The project will not only act as catalysts in scaling up MLC in the public health facilities at the primary health care (PHC) level but also will act as a pull-factor for the midwifery profession by creating employment for them and in the process, contributing to womens empowerment.
In addition to above, UNFPA is working towards the following objective: to improve availability, accessibility and utilization of SRHR services and climate change resilience and adaptability for the young and marginalized people of Bangladesh through engagement between youth, authorities and other key stakeholders at every level of governance. This objective was added following the youth-led movement in July-August 2024, which sparked significant socio-political changes and led to the establishment of a more youth-focused interim government. To achieve this objective, the programme will focus on the following outcomes:
Outcome 1: Youth-Led Advocacy for Inclusive Health and Climate Resilience
Outcome 2: Policy Reform and Engagement
Outcome 3: Addressing Social and Health Inequities
Outcome 4: Building Climate Resilience in Health

sector.narrative: Personnel development for population and reproductive health

description.narrative:
The Strengthening Midwifery-Led Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights project is implemented in the five most vulnerable districts of Bangladesh (Sunamganj, Chandpur, Noakhali, Bandarban and Dhaka). Quality assurance in midwifery education, midwifery mentorship, SRHR service delivery through the Friendship ship, climate change work, HGBV and introduction of STI services are all important achievements.
Achievement: The result of the project demonstrates the improvement of SRHR services in the project districts, more specifically in the Upazila Health Complexes (UzHCs), UHFWCs, and Dhaka urban slums where SRHR services are now available and accessible to the most vulnerable people. Normal Vaginal Deliveries (NVD) increased by 20% in the 4 District Hospitals (DH) and 31 UzHCs, ANC4 by 8%, management of post-partum haemorrhage (PPH) by 13% and management of Pre/Eclampsia by 27%. Post-Partum Family Planning (PPFP) services increased by 34% in the reporting period from the previous six months (April-September 2023). Midwives play an important role in delivering these services. 77% of NVDs in 31 UHCs and 86% in 4 DHs were conducted by midwives; the proportion of total NVDs conducted by midwives was high at all levels. Midwifery Education and Profession: A module on climate change and health, focused on SRHR was incorporated into the pre-registration midwifery diploma and in-service BSc courses; 20 master trainer midwifery faculty and 520 midwifery students from 15 institutions received training. 25 midwifery faculty and nurse managers were trained in Leadership and management and 25 officials of DGNM participated in a 3- day capacity-building workshop on disciplinary issues. A quality assurance system (QAS) for midwifery education was introduced with creating a national taskforce of 21 midwifery faculty for carrying forward the accreditation work. QA data was collected from 31 institutions. New midwifery faculty in 19 institutions received on-site support peer mentorhip. Significant steps were taken to advance the accreditation process for the midwifery education institutions: 5 institutes completed self-assessment and were visited by a new BNMC review committee to validate the self-assessment reports; 25 faculty received orientation on the accreditation guidelines. Workshops were held to finalize the standardized assessment system and clinical log book for the Bachelors in Midwifery programme, to further develop the MSc in Midwifery curriculum syllabus and to sensitise 150 midwifery faculty on the plans for the Masters and clinical mentorship programmes. The Massive Open Online Course (MOOC) in midwifery was revised and made available on the Canvas platform. 10 Young Midwife Leaders (YMLs) completed a two months-long English language course. UNFPAs advocacy to promote midwifery education in the hard-to-reach areas has prompted review of the national midwifery institution admission policy in February 2024 to reserve 1% quota for the students from the marginalized communities of the country, including Chittagong Hill Tract.
Midwifery-led Maternal Health: A significant milestone on creating 2000 midwifery posts for UHFWCs was achieved when MoHFW announced the creation of these posts. This is achieved by advocacy by both UNFPA and Sida. Advocacy at the local level was continued by the four District SRHR Officers who supported the district health authorities in improving the SRHR services, through implementation and tracking of the Annual District SRHR 8 Plan (ADSP). National support from all the three directorates (DGHS, DGNM, DGFP) was ensured for the same through the National SRHR Core Committee. District SRHR officers are coordinating with the central and local level authorities of the three directorates to functionalize at least 10 union level health facilities in each district by June 2024, to provide integrated midwife-led SRHR services. The District SRHR officers (DSRHO) continued offering onsite mentorship to midwives through the safe delivery App. A total of 496 mentorship sessions were undertaken. 18 midwives deployed at the district hospitals of Bandarban, Chandpur, and Sunamganj provided 66% ANC; 69% NVD; 72% PNC; and 52% PPFP services (out of all offered in the facilities). Among the total deliveries, caesarean sections accounted for 322, constituting 22% of the deliveries, which is much less than the national trend. Clinical mentorship played an important role in the increase in SRHR service provision in the newly operationalized UHFWCs. It was instrumental in improving the quality of clinical training for the midwifery students and practicing midwives in the 4 district hospitals and 5 selected UHCs of the intervention districts. 150 midwifery students got their clinical training from the 5 UHCs. Mentors also played a role in improving the readiness of the health facilities to offer midwifery-led SRHR services, including installation of 10 solar panels in the selected facilities. Based on Maternal Perinatal Death Surveillance and Response (MPDSR) Report of 2023, all four districts developed their MPDSR Action Plans, according to which all 4 district hospitals and 31 UHCs would be implementing MPDSR in 2024 as per the national guidelines. Midwifery-led SRHR Services: The Chandpur MCWC operationalized by the project conduct average 100 deliveries per month. The laboratory at the facility, conducts all basic SRHR investigations. From October 2023 to March 2024, a total of 1845 pathological tests were done which helped in identifying high-risk pregnancies, managing complications and ensuring timely referral. Partnering with Friendship took midwifery led SRHR services to the most vulnerable people through operationalizing 4 defunct UHFWCs in Jagannathpur union of Sunamgunj district and offering SRHR services through their ship hospital. A three-day health sector response to gender based violence (HGBV) training for 95 participants was held in two batches in Noakhali along with a day-long training on DHIS2 for HGBV reporting for 34 statisticians and Senior Staff Nurses (SSNs) from Noakhali and Chandpur districts. 255 SGBV survivors were reported from the two districts, who received medical care from their respective UHCs and DH. The Triple Elimination Programme, designed to provide screening services by utilizing Rapid Testing Kits for HIV, syphilis, and Hepatitis-B during the Antenatal Care (ANC) to effectively manage Maternal to Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B, was initiated in Chandpur district by deploying a lab assistant at Haimchor, Chandpur. During the last 6 months there were a total of 336,672 VIA screenings done in the 4 district hospitals and 31 upazila health complexes. Of these, 1,273 women were identified as VIA positive. From October 2023 to March 2024, a total of 438 colposcopy services were provided in the four district hospitals. Among them, 108 received thermal ablation as required and eligible, 14 received LEEP service and 16 individuals were diagnosed 9 as cervical cancer patients. Ten cancer patients were supported with treatment services from a specialized hospital in Dhaka.
Gender Empowerment: The project focuses on SRHR services delivered by midwives and is incrementally developing a sound and a sustainable network of gender inclusiveness and equality, from education to employment for midwives. This projects emphasis on capacitating the young female midwifery workforce, enabling them to perform their whole scope of practice and to raise their voices locally and nationally is taking a strong step towards gender equality.
Climate-change: How climate change affects SRHR is part of the midwifery diploma curriculum but also part of the future masters in midwifery. The current project has integrated the impact of climate-change on SRHR into its design, keeping in mind the variability of climate-change impact on SRHR by geographies and communities and the different pathways by which it affects SRHR. More specifically, climate change work has been initiated in Sunamganj district. Two upazilas, Dowarabazar and Sunamganj Sadar have been selected for the pilot. Non random listing of pregnant women and adolescent girls have been done for household selection. Schools and madrasahs have been identified where awareness-raising sessions will be initiated. A comprehensive baseline assessment is underway which aims to explore climate-change knowledge, experience, perceptions of risk, efficacy and impacts on health and SRHR. The Minimum Initial Services Package (MISP) on SRHR and GBV services is being translated into Bengali and will be submitted for endorsement by the government that will be introduced in all four project districts as response and preparedness to address the vulnerability of people, particularly women and girls, to SRHR and GBV due to exacerbated climate-change events and disasters. Existing disaster management platforms are being explored in Sunamganj to integrate SRHR and GBV prevention and response as part of readiness. For the two selected upazilas, local structures have been identified which can serve as shelters during flash floods. The 18 union disaster management committees and 58 community support groups have been revitalized.
